s1.syndrome_frame: Acute chest pain with pleuritic and intermittent characteristics, associated with diaphoresis and elevated troponin levels, in a young adult with recent onset of systemic inflammation
salient_findings: Pleuritic pain worsened by sitting forward
Extensive patchy late gadolinium enhancement on cardiac magnetic resonance imaging
key_facts: 2-day history of intermittent, sharp, central chest pain
No family history of cardiovascular disease
ECG showed sinus rhythm with benign early repolarization
Negative serum viral and autoantibody screens

shortlist.label: Myocarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated troponin levels, recent onset of systemic inflammation, and cardiac magnetic resonance imaging findings of myocardial edema and late gadolinium enhancement

shortlist.label: Acute coronary syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated high-sensitivity troponin T and atypical chest pain

shortlist.label: Inflammatory bowel disease-associated cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Recent diagnosis of ulcerative colitis and cardiac involvement suggested by elevated troponin levels and cardiac magnetic resonance imaging findings

shortlist.label: Pericarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Pleuritic chest pain and elevated C-reactive protein, although no pericardial effusion was found on echocardiography

shortlist.label: Ulcerative colitis-associated myocarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Recent diagnosis of ulcerative colitis and cardiac involvement suggested by elevated troponin levels and cardiac magnetic resonance imaging findings, providing a specific link between the patient's condition and cardiac disease

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with sharp, central chest pain, diaphoresis, and elevated high-sensitivity troponin T, along with the cardiac magnetic resonance imaging findings of mild systolic dysfunction, hypokinesia of the anterolateral and inferolateral segments, and extensive patchy late gadolinium enhancement, are consistent with myocarditis. The absence of pericardial effusion and the distribution of late gadolinium enhancement also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Acute coronary syndrome
rejected.why: The patient's young age, lack of family history of cardiovascular disease, and the presence of stage 2 finger clubbing make this diagnosis less likely. Additionally, the cardiac magnetic resonance imaging findings do not suggest coronary artery disease.

rejected.label: Inflammatory bowel disease-associated cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: While the patient has a recent diagnosis of ulcerative colitis, the cardiac findings are more consistent with an acute inflammatory process such as myocarditis rather than a cardiomyopathy.

rejected.label: Pericarditis
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings do not suggest pericarditis, as there is no pericardial effusion and the pain is not typically relieved by sitting forward.

rejected.label: Ulcerative colitis-associated myocarditis
rejected.why: While the patient has ulcerative colitis, this is not a recognized medical condition, and the diagnosis of myocarditis is more appropriate based on the clinical and imaging findings.
